js.ha.update.intro: Home Assistant has a new version of Vedetta. Vedetta does not update itself: the update is made from the Updates page of Home Assistant.
js.ha.update.step1: The Updates page of Home Assistant opens: there you choose whether and when to install.
js.ha.update.step2: While it installs, Vedetta stops and restarts with the new version: for a few minutes you will see “Disconnected” here.
js.ha.update.step3: Home Assistant can make a backup first: it is an option in its window.
js.ha.update.step4: When it is done, reload this page to use the new version. Your data and settings stay.

js.ha.export.vlan.adv_text: Only for people with several networks (VLANs). The normal export does not need it: leave it as it is.
js.ha.export.vlan.btn_idle_sub: Tap to check that Home Assistant has it
js.ha.export.vlan.btn_ok_sub: Ready to include. Tap to remove.
js.ha.export.vlan.info_label: What must be set up in Home Assistant first
js.ha.export.vlan.pop_s1_d: A router, controller or access point that tracks the clients
js.ha.export.vlan.pop_s2_d: The presence entities of the clients, not disabled
js.ha.export.vlan.pop_s3_d: Choose the networks or clients in the integration: Vedetta reads only those
js.ha.export.vlan.g_lead: Do the steps in order. Each one says where to go, what to do and what you must see. If you do not see it, read “If it does not work” under the same step.
js.ha.export.vlan.notneeded: This option is only for people with several networks (VLANs). If you do not need it, close the guide and export: the export works anyway.
js.ha.export.vlan.why_none: I found no network devices in Home Assistant.
js.ha.export.vlan.why_none_sub: If you need it, follow the steps below.
js.ha.export.vlan.why_noha: Vedetta cannot read Home Assistant right now.
js.ha.export.vlan.why_noha_sub: If you need it, try again in a moment.
js.ha.export.vlan.ready_1: the integration shows nothing in red
js.ha.export.vlan.ready_2: in “Entities” you see the devices you want to include
js.ha.export.vlan.ready_3: none of them has the ⊘ symbol
js.ha.export.vlan.s1_t: Find the integration of your router
js.ha.export.vlan.s1_todo: In the “Configured” list look for the integration of your router, controller or access point (type the maker's name in “Search integrations”). If it is not there, tap “+ Add integration” at the bottom right, search for it and follow the steps.
js.ha.export.vlan.s1_see: Its card, with nothing in red.
js.ha.export.vlan.s1_b1_s: The card has a red border and says “Failed setup, will retry”
js.ha.export.vlan.s1_b1_r: The integration cannot connect to the device. Open it and check address, user and password. The device must be on and reachable.
js.ha.export.vlan.s1_b2_r: It may be hidden: tap the filter icon at the top right and tick “Show disabled integrations” and “Show ignored integrations”. If you find it, open it and enable it again from its ⋮ menu.
js.ha.export.vlan.s1_b4_s: Your router has no integration at all
js.ha.export.vlan.s1_b4_r: That is fine: leave the button off, the export works anyway.
js.ha.export.vlan.s2_t: Turn on the detection of devices
js.ha.export.vlan.s2_todo: Open the integration and look for the “Configure” button (or its options). Turn on the option that tracks the devices connected to the network: it is usually called “track clients” or “presence detection”, the name changes from one integration to another. Save.
js.ha.export.vlan.s2_see: After a few minutes the devices appear as entities (step 3).
js.ha.export.vlan.s2_b1_r: That integration does not track the devices: it is not suitable for this.
js.ha.export.vlan.s3_t: Check that the trackers are active
js.ha.export.vlan.s3_todo: Type “device_tracker” in the search box at the top (“Search … entities”).
js.ha.export.vlan.s3_see: The list of your network devices, each with its name and none with the ⊘ symbol on the right.
js.ha.export.vlan.s3_b1_s: The list is empty or devices are missing
js.ha.export.vlan.s3_b1_r: Disabled entities are hidden: tap “Filters” › “Status”. “Enabled” is already ticked and hides the disabled ones. Untick it and tick “Disabled”: you will see only the disabled ones, with the ⊘ symbol. Then tick “Enabled” again.
js.ha.export.vlan.s3_b2_s: Opening an entity you read “This entity is disabled.”
js.ha.export.vlan.s3_b2_r: Tap the gear at the top right, turn on the “Enabled” switch and press “Update”. Wait a minute.
js.ha.export.vlan.s3_b3_s: You read “Cannot change status. Disabled by config entry.”
js.ha.export.vlan.s3_b3_r: The integration turned it off, not you. Tap “Open device settings” and enable the device. If the integration itself is disabled, enable it (step 1).
js.ha.export.vlan.s3_b4_r: That device is not connected now or the integration does not see it. Check the integration's card (step 1).
js.ha.export.vlan.s4_todo: Leave on only the Wi-Fi networks or the devices you want in the report. Vedetta reads only the active trackers.
js.ha.export.vlan.s4_see: In the Entities page only the devices you chose are left.
js.ha.export.vlan.s4_b1_r: In the options turn on the wired devices too, if the integration has this option.
js.ha.export.vlan.s5_todo: Tap “Include VLAN data”: Vedetta checks right away whether it finds the devices.
js.ha.export.vlan.s5_see: The button turns green and says how many devices it found. Then export.
